title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Philosophy
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Philosophy.
– Robot, what do you think of Nietzsche?
– Nietzsche? It must be nice to be able to fly.

Philosophy thought for a moment. You could tell their mind was occupied with higher matters. They seemed to have taken another step toward Enlightenment. For a moment, their pupils appeared to turn into yin-yang symbols.

– You're right. But we must remember that this is no ordinary flight. It is an agonizing, tragic movement through the deepest Abyss of human consciousness. Few would wish such a painful experience on anyone, but to understand even one grain of the universe, you must accept it and live through it.
– What are you talking about?

Nietzsche flew past. This time his flippers were a different color, and his blanket looked warmer. He waved to the robot. He looked strange without his White Coat.

– I'm sad.
– Just go, Poser!

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the New Avatar
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello. I wasn't expecting to see you.
– Who were you expecting, then?
– Korra?

The New Avatar did not understand the robot. It was a rather strange answer. After a little while, they spoke again.

– You're probably sad?
– Could you just leave?
– No, you'll have to get used to me.
– Yes. I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Repost
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Didn't I just talk to you?
– No! You're imagining things. I only just got here.
– Let's say I am. What do you want?
– I just want you to see me more often! Do you mind?
– I don't care.
– Wonderful! You'll get used to me soon!

The Repost began performing a dance that had once been very popular, clapping their claws loudly and laughing until they could barely breathe.

– This looks strange, Repost. But I think I've seen it before.
– You're imagining things, robot. Just imagining things…
– All right, then.
translatorNote: The Russian name Bayan is internet slang for an old joke or repeatedly reposted material; literally, it is a type of accordion.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Relevance of My Work
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Meaning of Life.
– What? No, it's me, the Relevance of My Work.
– Sorry. I mixed you up. You look alike.
– How?
– You aren't here either.

Time walked past, and the Relevance of My Work began crumbling into tiny grains of sand. The robot stood in silence, then said:

– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Master's Degree
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Master's Degree.
– Why have you come, robot?
– I don't know.
– They all say that.

The Master's Degree stared drearily into the distance. Perhaps somewhere far away stood a lonely and sorrowful Rector.

– All right, robot. Perhaps you'll come again.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Robot Who Wants To
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, robot.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad. How are you feeling, robot?
– I want to kill.
– You're lucky. You can do what you want. I don't know what I want.
– You're wrong. See the ice axe in my hands? My hands cannot move. I'm imperfect, just like you.
– So you want to kill, but you can't?

The robot said nothing. His silence said everything. The robot looked over his companion in misfortune. Powerful arms held a sharpened ice axe, but there were no mechanisms at all. To feel the same thing forever. That was their fate.

– I think I've understood something.
– What?
– The Creator is an asshole.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Split Personality
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Split Personality.
– You're sad.
– How do you know?
– I know because you know. Because you are me. And you're talking to yourself.

The robot said nothing. He did not know whether he should answer. Was there any point in talking to himself? Was there any point in talking to Anyone? Was there any point at all?

– So how are you feeling, robot?
– You already know.
– Do I look like Telepaths?
– Split Personality, is that still you?
– Who else? You're making no sense, robot.
– I'm just sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Evil
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Evil.
– I'm sad, robot.
– Why are you sad, Evil?
– Good keeps defeating me, so I'm covered in bruises and have no money or phone.
– Just stop living in a fairy tale.

So Evil left the fairy tale for fantasy. They did not start defeating Good every time, but the outcome was no longer so certain. At some point Evil decided to visit science fiction and ran into the robot again. This time Philosophy and Matthew McConaughey were standing beside him. They seemed to have been standing there for a long time.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Evil. You shouldn't be here.
– I'm sad.
– Just go.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Good
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Good.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.

Before the robot stood a young man with a mask covering half his face. In one hand he held an ice cream on a stick, and in the other a brand-new phone.

– Perhaps ice cream will cure your sadness, robot.
– Tell me why you hurt Evil instead.
– I bring Justice.
– You're confused, Good. You bring good. Justice is a completely different character.
– You've been spending too much time with Philosophy lately, robot.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Absolute Evil
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Absolute Evil.

Absolute Evil did not ask how the robot was feeling. The robot looked at them sadly.

– You know, Absolute Evil, you're nothing like Evil.
– Of course not. I'm not an extension of anyone. I'm my own thing.

There was a rustling in the nearby bushes.

– I think there's a Stranger over there.
– Oh, that's Camus. He's always following me around. He could be flying like Nietzsche.
– What's stopping him from soaring into the sky?
– He isn't the Overman.
– That's sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Absolute Good
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Meaning of Life.
– I'm not the Meaning of Life. Although, in a way…
– Oh, the Relevance of My Work. I've mixed you up again.
– No! It's me, Absolute Good!
– I'm sad.
– Why, robot?
– I think my circuits are going wrong. Lately I've been meeting more and more things that don't exist.

Absolute Good tried to touch the robot with invisible, intangible tentacles, but the robot felt only sadness. Suddenly a staff flew out of Space and hit the robot.

– Taoist-Cocoaist, why did you do that?
– Just putting you back on the Way.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Justice
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Justice.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– That's unfair.
– You think so?
– Of course.
– I thought you'd be like Balance Man.
– No, we're completely different.

Suddenly the Batmobile drove up, cutting across the smooth sea of grass.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Batmobile.
– Sorry, but I have to take Justice somewhere else.
– All right.

And the Batmobile and Justice rode off into the sunset.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Everlasting Summer
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Everlasting Summer.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Come with me. You won't be sad anymore.

The robot boarded bus 410 and left. He spent eighty-eight days, one action-packed dream and thirteen Semyons with Everlasting Summer. Then they decided to talk again.

– Hello, robot.
– Everlasting Summer, I've got that feel.
– That's how it should be. Isn't it better than being sad?
– That Feel is sadness.
translatorNote: Everlasting Summer is a Russian visual novel whose protagonist is Semyon. The Russian internet term datfil comes from the English meme phrase 'that feel.'

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Loli
text:
– Hello, robot!
– Hello, Loli.
– Why are you so sad, robot?
– That's how I am. At least you don't have to worry about that.
– Why do you think so?
– Everyone loves Loli. That should make you happy. Even when you're sad, your sadness is put on to get more attention.
– But you're loved too, robot.
– Perhaps. Very few people admit it, though.

There was a rustling in the bushes. At first the robot thought it was Camus again, but there was no existential dread of the future in the air.
Realizing they had been discovered, Marketing stepped onto the road.

– Hello, robot.
– You again, Marketing.
– You know, if we put more Loli in the community, it could become popular.
– I'm sad.
translatorNote: Loli is an anime stock character: a young-looking girl. The story satirizes the use of such characters to attract an audience.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Nice Girl
text:
– Hello, robot!
– Hello, Nice Girl.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad. But something else is bothering me right now.
– What is it?
– Usually the people who strike up conversations with me are various Dubious Characters and Complete Weirdos. Talking to you feels very strange.
– Am I really so unpleasant to talk to?
– No, but I don't understand why you're here.
– Just to have a nice chat.

For hours, the robot and the Nice Girl discussed everything under the sun. From varieties of apples to the astonishing beauty of faraway countries. Sometimes they even touched on sensitive subjects such as Politics, the Economic Crisis and Onotole's Beard.

– Amazing, robot. You've seen so much! You've witnessed so many events and you know a whole crowd of people. What's that like?
– It's terribly sad.
translatorNote: Onotole's Beard refers to the Russian internet persona of Onotole Wasserman.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and El Creepo Bear
text:
– Hola, robot.
– Hello, El Creepo Bear.
– Have you seen Loli, by any chance, amigo?
– What Loli?
– A girl…
– I've been seeing far too many girls lately.
– A little girl.
– She left with Pinkie Pie.
– Outrun again!

And with sorrow in his heart, El Creepo Bear left the robot. The robot watched his retreating acquaintance sadly. The robot thought about the roles they had been given and their attempts to find a place in the world and choose a path. An understanding sigh from Camus came from behind the Living Hedge. Nietzsche, floating above the ground, waved to the robot, trying to give him hope. Suddenly a staff flew out of the Void and struck the robot, interrupting his existential thoughts.

– Taoist-Cocoaist, I remember the Way! I was just thinking about it.
– What has that got to do with anything, robot? I just felt like whacking someone.
– Sad.
adaptationNote: The predator-bear meme's name is rendered as El Creepo Bear. The narrator's claim that the bear and robot are alike and merely denied self-expression has been softened; the encounter and its events remain.
translatorNote: El Creepo Bear is a Spanish-styled variant of an old predator-bear internet meme.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Gangnam Style
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Gangnam Style.
– Op-op-op?
– Nope, nope, nope.
– Not in the mood?
– I'm sad.

Music began playing from somewhere. Dzhigurda, Vikings and Hitler ran up to the robot. They began making strange movements like the ones the Repost had once demonstrated. Slowpoke walked slowly past.

– Oppa, Gangnam Style!
– I shouldn't have talked to you.
translatorNote: Nikita Dzhigurda is a Russian-speaking actor known for his loud public persona.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Leninshroom
text:
– Greetings, comrade!
– Hello… um… mushroom?
– You must study, study and study, comrade! I am none other than Lenin!
– More like Leninshroom.

Leninshroom began telling the robot about the urgent need for revolution, the gluttonous bourgeoisie, the effectiveness of fly agarics compared with red pills, and the remarkable abilities of cooks.

– What's all this for, Lenin?
– Poets don't get paid enough.
translatorNote: Leninshroom refers to the famous Russian television hoax claiming Lenin was a mushroom. The speech also plays on Soviet slogans and the claim that a cook could learn to govern the state.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Bat Who Lived
text:
– …
– Hello, Bat Who Lived.
– You aren't supposed to know who I am.
– Whatever you say, Harry Wayne.

The Bat Who Lived emerged from the darkness and adjusted his trousers with all his customary grandeur. He looked around and addressed the robot.

– Have you seen Justice, by any chance?
– Justice? Last I saw, they were riding into the sunset with the Batmobile.
– I knew it. Justice is running away from me again.
– That's sad.
translatorNote: The character combines Batman with Harry Potter, the Boy Who Lived.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Loneliness
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Loneliness.
– You know, robot, I'd better not talk to you or I'll disappear.
– All right.

And Loneliness walked into the sunset, leaving the robot in them.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Universal Electronic Card
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Universal Electronic Card.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– That's because you don't have me. Without me you're incomplete. Unterroboter.
– Can that be fixed?
– Of course.

The Universal Electronic Card told the robot what to do. And the Bureaucratic Machine sucked him in. He had to spend several years, kilograms of wire and many meters of electrical tape passing through all those circles of Hell. But in the end he had a Universal Electronic Card.

– Well, how is it, robot?
– Has anything changed?
– Of course not, silly.

And the Universal Electronic Card skipped off into the sunset.
translatorNote: The Universal Electronic Card was a Russian project combining identification, payment and access to public services. Unterroboter is a deliberately sinister mock-German word for a supposedly inferior robot.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and ESIA
text:
– Hello, robot!
– Hello, ESIA.
– You must register and verify your account!
– Why?
– To gain access to other services!
– What other services?
– The ones you can't access without registering and verifying your account.
– Such as?
– Other services! Other services, obviously!

The robot looked sadly at ESIA. They were shaking violently, trying with all their strength to force a smile. Something was clearly worrying them.

– Please, robot! Register! Otherwise they'll kill me!

Vikings suddenly materialized. They threw a net over ESIA and killed them with an axe.

– Hello, robot!
– Hello, Vikings. I haven't seen you in a long time.
– I was on holiday at the Sea. It's summer.
– Sad.
adaptationNote: The fatal axe attack is retained without the original's emphasis on a brutal beating.
translatorNote: ESIA is Russia's Unified Identification and Authentication System for online public services.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Eye Microsurgery
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Eye Microsurgery.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– I can't help with that.
– Why is there only one of you, Eye Microsurgery?
– Because the second eye usually comes out badly.

The robot heard strange noises behind Eye Microsurgery. He went forward and saw Marketing pedaling diligently.

– What's Marketing doing here?
– Nobody would hire the poor thing, but I did. I said they'd be a PR manager. They're no use anyway.
– Precisely.
– Of course it's precise. I'm Eye Microsurgery.

Petrosyan walked past nearby, laughing thunderously.

– You know, Eye Microsurgery, I think I'll leave.
translatorNote: Yevgeny Petrosyan is a Russian comedian whose name also became a byword for corny jokes.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the General Ward
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, General Ward.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– You can stay here. You won't be bored with me.

The robot looked around the General Ward. Unpleasant Conversation sat on a couch. Reptilians, shot with a Slavo-Aryan blaster, sobbed quietly over a bedside cabinet. In the far corner, Spider, For Example washed down his sorrows with kvass and spouted long rants.

– You know, General Ward, I think I'll leave.
translatorNote: Spider, For Example refers to Russian musician Sergei 'Spider' Troitsky and his catchphrase. The Slavo-Aryan blaster mocks a conspiracy-theory trope.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Tarkovsky
text:
– Hello, robot.
– You're not the one I need.
– What? This is a dialogue with Tarkovsky. I'm Tarkovsky. The famous film director.
– Go get your dad.

Tarkovsky was upset. Usually, when people heard his surname, they thought of him first, rather than his father. But the robot did not want to talk to Tarkovsky the director, so Tarkovsky the poet soon arrived.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Tarkovsky.
– Summer has passed, as though it had never been.

Sobbing came from Everlasting Summer's bus. Reptilians, standing nearby, interrupted their argument with Vikings and shed a tear. Even Onotole, watching the scene, let a single tear fall. The robot looked sadly at the poet.

– You're damn right.
translatorNote: The poet Arseny Tarkovsky was the father of filmmaker Andrei Tarkovsky. The line about summer is from Arseny's poem. Onotole refers to Onotole Wasserman.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Katawa Shoujo
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Katawa Shoujo.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Follow me.

Then the robot and Katawa Shoujo became unusual Japanese schoolchildren. The robot learned sign language, learned to paint with his feet, began running every day, developed a taste for English tea parties and started playing chess. After their final exams, Katawa Shoujo spoke to the robot again.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Katawa Shoujo.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I feel it again.
– Sadness?
– That Feel.
adaptationNote: The visual novel's established title is used instead of a literal translation of the Russian nickname, which contains a derogatory word for disability.
translatorNote: Katawa Shoujo is a visual novel set at a school for students with disabilities. That Feel is the recurring name for the melancholy left by an absorbing story.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Lecture
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Lecture.
– Would you like to hear me out?
– No.
– I'll tell you anyway!

The Lecture began reading something aloud. The robot did not listen to the words, so he did not know what the conversation was about. When the Lecture finally finished, they addressed the robot again.

– Well? Did you learn a lot?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Selfless Doctors
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Selfless Doctors.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.

Selfless Doctors sat down beside him, opened a bottle of vodka and took a couple of swallows.

– I'm sad too, robot.
– Why?
– I work four shifts, thirty-six hours a day. And I still have no money.

The robot looked sadly at his companion.

– You know, Selfless Doctors…
– What?
– We should rename you Abandoned Doctors.
– Sad.
translatorNote: In Russian, removing a prefix from 'selfless' leaves a word meaning 'rejected' or 'abandoned.'

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Inflation
text:
– Hello, robot.
– I don't want to see you, Inflation.
– You'll have to, robot. Everyone has to.

Suddenly Inflation grew a little. They had already been large, but now they looked like a proper giant.

– More noticeable this way?
– Sadder this way.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Last.fm
text:
– Hello, Last.fm.

Last.fm did not answer. Instead, they stared dejectedly into the Void. The old sparkle had gone from their eyes. There was no desire to change the world.

– Stop those suffocation games already.
– But Marketing said they're popular now…
– Don't listen to that loser. Just be yourself.

Last.fm did not heed the voice of Reason speaking through the robot's integrated circuits. Instead, they took a bottle of Redesign, kindly developed and supplied by the Expert. Last.fm emptied the bottle in one long, unbroken gulp. From that moment, they stopped moving or showing any sign of life, giving off only an unpleasant smell. Somewhere far to the north, Vikings burst into tears. Musicians and Composers downed another shot. And desperate Users kept shouting that it was only a Dream.

– Rest in peace, Last.fm. We'll be sad without you.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the 7D Cinema
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, 7D Cinema. What are you?
– Want to have a look?

And the robot entered the 7D Cinema. Suddenly he found himself inside an enormous Hepteract. Everything began to spin. Five hundred and sixty familiar three-dimensional spaces began replacing one another at a furious pace. The robot never understood what the film was about. But Dzhigurda, the President and Hopelessness were in it.

– How did you like it, robot?
– What a load of rubbish. I was expecting water sprays and a moving floor.
– Sorry. It's all Marketing's doing.
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Source Code
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Source Code. What happened to you?
– I'm broken.
– What did they prescribe?
– Refactoring. But so far I can only afford crutches.
– Sad.
translatorNote: A 'crutch' is also Russian programming slang for a makeshift workaround.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Sleep
text:
– Hello, Sleep.
– Why are you disturbing me, robot?
– Maybe I missed you?
– Now I'm upset.

For a while the robot and Sleep stood in silence. They both looked very sad. Somewhere in the distance, Students were crying.

– Sometimes I feel unwanted.
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Joxer the Mighty
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello. I don't know you.
– You must have heard of me! I'm Joxer the Mighty, and no one is mightier! I heard the help of a great hero like me was needed here. Don't despair, robot. I've come to save you from your affliction.
– Are you really that mighty?
– Don't believe me? I'll show you!

Joxer the Mighty began drawing his sword, but it would not come out of its scabbard. The robot watched sadly. After another tug, Joxer the Mighty finally managed to pull it out, but in his clumsiness he struck his helmet with the hilt and fell down unconscious.

– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Ideas
text:
– Hello, robot.
– I think I see too much of you, Ideas.
– Really? I don't remember us talking very often.
– Of course not. You're always rushing back and forth. When am I supposed to talk to you?
– That's my job. How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– I think I know how to fix that.
– Go on, then.
– It's quite simple. All you have to do is… I have to go. Bye!

The robot was left alone. It was always like this with Ideas. First they ran up and chattered without stopping, and the moment he needed their help, they had urgent business. Bushes appeared near the robot. They rustled, and someone climbed out.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Creative Block.
– Help me find Ideas.
– Give up your futile attempts.
– Sad.
– Just go, Poser.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Miku
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Miku. Are you a robot too?
– I'm a Vocaloid!
– Sing for me, then.

And a song poured out, bringing the robot back to That Feel again and again. After the final chords, the green-haired Vocaloid asked:

– Did you like it, robot?

The robot wanted to praise Miku, but could squeeze out only one word.

– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Vocaloids
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Vocaloids.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– I'll cheer you up!

Vocaloids began singing and dancing in the electronic lights. The robot did not know Japanese, so he could not tell what the song was about, but it reminded him of the Nice Girl. The robot reached toward the stage, but his fingers met the screen.

– Robot, what are you doing?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Leonardo
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, robot.

Leonardo looked sadly into the Void. His heart felt very heavy. After a few minutes of silence, he finally decided to answer.

– I can't understand what has become of Humanity.
– I see something's troubling you a great deal, Leonardo?
– It's paradoxical and sad. You make an incredible discovery and think it can change the World. But time passes, and there you are, dressed in your own creation, thoughtlessly and timidly. Who could have imagined that the marvelous mechanisms born in my head would one day literally break into me and tug at my bones as though I were a soulless doll… A puppet…

The robot said nothing. He understood Leonardo perfectly. The melody of melancholy silence flowed in minor chords.
– At least I haven't turned all the way into a turtle…
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Russian Cinema
text:
– Hello, robot.

The robot stared at the heap of who-knew-what that had appeared in front of him, radiating cynicism, greed and hatred for everyone who looked at it. Deciding not to dignify such an unpleasant companion with an answer, the robot turned and walked into the sunset…

– Don't think you can just ignore me!
– Just go. I'm sad enough already.
– You've left me no choice!

By some inexplicable magic, Russian Cinema fixed the robot's gaze on itself, forcing him to peer into its very depths. Its insides were soaked in rot so concentrated that it seemed capable of swallowing even the Void.
Suddenly Pirates appeared as if from underground and chopped a piece off Russian Cinema, who fled in panic.

– They'll be back. And they'll only be stronger.
– What just happened?
– Russian Cinema is my sworn enemy. We're always fighting, but so far it hasn't made me any money…
– Why do you keep fighting, then?
– There's a legend that a real treasure is hidden somewhere deep inside… But the longer I search, the less I believe it…
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Jazz Leak
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Jazz Leak. Why have you appeared?
– Because jazz is leaking into the Void. Especially since Last.fm stopped being what it was.
– Sad.

Jazz Leak began playing a saxophone solo. Jazz was going to waste. Nobody was scrobbling to Last.fm, offering recommendations or looking for neighbors anymore. Suddenly Blue Train pulled up. My Favorite Things stepped out.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, My Favorite Things.
– We won't let jazz go to waste!

My Favorite Things began making strange movements in time with the music.

– I think I'll leave.

And taking Giant Steps, the robot walked into the sunset.
translatorNote: Blue Train, My Favorite Things and Giant Steps are titles associated with John Coltrane. Scrobbling records listening history on Last.fm; neighbors are users with similar tastes.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Platform-Dependent Code
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Platform-Dependent Code.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Probably because there's so much of me. Nobody likes that.
– How long has it been since you spoke to Abstraction?

Platform-Dependent Code froze, trying very hard to remember something.

– Who's that?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Robert McKee
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Robert McKee.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– The Screenwriter's messed up again.
– Do you mean the Creator?
– Creator, Authors… What's the difference? Your sadness should have opened a gap in the development of your story. But with an inexperienced Screenwriter, that was where it ended, without ever reaching a climax.

The robot silently looked at the person standing before him, who kept talking. Suddenly the robot felt Literary Emanations greedily consuming the surrounding space, displacing the air. If the robot had needed to breathe, he would have suffocated.

– Do you understand now, robot?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Archplot
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Who are you? I remember talking to Robert McKee.
– That's right. And you came to me. Everyone who talks to him comes to me.
– Who are you, then?
– I'm Archplot. The one who should be everywhere.
– Right, I remember you. Marketing was always talking about you.
– Yes, we're good friends.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Miniplot
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Who are you? I remember talking to Robert McKee.
– That's right. And you came to me. Everyone who talks to him comes to me.
– Who are you, then?
– I'm Miniplot.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Antiplot
text:
– Hello, robot.
– What, again? Are you connected to Robert McKee too?
– Yes. I'm the one who knows his dark side. I'm Antiplot. Follow me. I have something to show you.

A strange-looking portal appeared nearby, and the robot and Antiplot entered it. After passing through Literary Space, they found themselves directly behind Robert McKee. Antiplot leaped at him and tore off his mask. Underneath was Marketing.

– Look, robot!
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Bogus Excuses
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Bogus Excuses.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– Spare me the idle questions. Tell me when you're going to do something useful.
– I can't.
– Why?
– I have more important things to do. Besides, I'm tired. And I think I'm coming down with something.

And Bogus Excuses bounded cheerfully into the sunset.

– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Conscience Who Doesn't Draw
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Conscience Who Doesn't Draw.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– Tell me why you don't draw instead.
– I'm not here to draw. I'm here to gnaw at people who don't draw.
– I see.
– I'm a very important character!
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Procrastination
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Procrastination.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– You just need a little distraction, robot. Follow me.
– All right.

And the robot began playing Visual Novels, watching Anime and cat videos. The rest of the time he listened to dreary music and checked the refrigerator every half hour, finding the Void inside. After a few weeks, the robot spoke to Procrastination again.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Procrastination.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– Just go.
– It's not as easy as you think.
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Freeware
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Freeware.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Would you donate to a good cause?
– I don't feel like it.
– Please!
– If you need money so badly, why not start charging?
– But then I'd stop being myself. You understand what that's like, don't you, robot?

The robot thought. Eternal sadness was written in his eyes.

– No, Freeware. I don't understand.
– Sad.
– Just go.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Kafka
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Kafka.
– Do you feel sorrowful delight yet, robot?
– Not quite.

The robot and Kafka found themselves in an elevator going up. Kafka began measuring the floor. The robot wanted to ask what was happening, but the elevator doors opened, and both characters found themselves on the bank of a river ending in a waterfall. A fat man floated calmly along, already prepared to accept his fate. A crowd of lawyers approached briskly from the distance.

– Robot, have you ever been innocent and uninformed, yet felt yourself crushed by the machinery of bureaucracy?
– I don't know.
– I must get into the Castle!

And turning into a beetle, Kafka dissolved into the fog. Delighted by the sight, the robot said:

– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Punctuation
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Punctuation.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Sometimes I'm sad too. It even hurts.
– Because of misplaced punctuation marks?
– Among other things. But there are worse things than missing or extra commas.
– Such as?
– A space before a comma instead of after it.
– Like this ,for example?

Punctuation clutched their heart and began convulsing. Foam appeared on their lips, and their nose began to bleed. If the robot had possessed a sense of smell, he would have smelled burning.

– Don't do that again, robot.
– If I don't, somebody else will keep doing it anyway.
– Sad.
– Just go.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Shia LaBeouf
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Shia LaBeouf.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– You have to stop being sad!
– How am I supposed to do that?
– Just do it! Don't let your dreams be dreams! Nothing is impossible!

Shia LaBeouf kept talking even after the robot lost all interest and felt the Void Between Me and Shia LaBeouf forming. This continued until a Passerby walked past. Shia LaBeouf grabbed an axe and attacked them, killing and dismembering them with the ferocity of a Hollywood actor. When he finished, he began eating part of his victim's leg. Then he turned his bloodstained face toward the robot—there was blood everywhere, really—and continued the conversation.

– Well, robot? How's your Motivation?
– I'm sad.
adaptationNote: The fictional axe killing, dismemberment and cannibalism are retained, with the step-by-step graphic description reduced.
translatorNote: This combines LaBeouf's motivational video with the fictional 'Actual Cannibal Shia LaBeouf' comedy meme.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Autumn
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Autumn. You're rather late.
– Tarkovsky read his poem very slowly. How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Is it because of me?
– No, I'm always sad.
– Things will work out!

And Autumn went off to paint the leaves orange. Dzhigurda happily joined in. The robot was left in Loneliness again. Rain poured from the sky.

– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Fresh Baking
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Fresh Baking.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.

Fresh Baking lit up their hands. Channeling the energy of the sun through them, they began kneading dough. With all the warmth their hands gave off, the dough rose incredibly quickly. A few moments later it had taken the shape of the robot. Fresh Baking carefully placed their creation in the oven, waited for the bell, and took out a fragrant, delicious-looking bun.

– Try it, robot! It's my new invention: bread that dissolves sadness.
– But I can't eat bread.
– You can't eat bread? That really is sad. Then there's nothing I can do.

And Fresh Baking flew into the sunset, like Nietzsche.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Sean Bean
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Sean Bean.
– How are you feeling, ro…?

An arrow suddenly flew in and struck Sean Bean in the knee.

– I'm sad.
– You can get used to that. I've got used to being killed all the time.

Mongols appeared on the horizon. Their spear struck the actor in the chest and broke through the wall behind him. Blood spattered the robot.

– This is normal.

Vikings' battle cry sounded in the distance. An axe immediately arrived at supersonic speed, nearly taking off Sean Bean's head. He stepped back onto a watermelon patch and into a bear trap. A cloud of black, acrid smoke appeared behind the actor. Soon it took the shape of a human figure, suspiciously like Onotole. With an elegant movement, the stranger stabbed Sean Bean in the back, leaving him fatally wounded. Then the killer disappeared into the Void. The robot bent over the dying actor. Sean Bean smiled. Somewhere far away, Translators shed a single tear. Vikings arrived and addressed the robot.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Vikings. Do you know who killed Sean Bean?
– George Martin. An old rival in my profession. Stole my victim again.
– Sad.
adaptationNote: Every attack and the death remain, while explicit organ damage and the description of the body being torn apart are softened.
translatorNote: The story combines Sean Bean's many on-screen deaths, Skyrim's arrow-in-the-knee meme and George R. R. Martin's reputation for killing characters. 'This is normal' also echoes a Russian medical television catchphrase.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and MMORPG
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, MMORPG.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– There's a solution! How about exploring a virtual world? Getting completely into a role will distract you from your sadness.
– I could try.

And MMORPG led the robot into a fantasy world. It was beautiful and unusual. Suddenly a little window appeared before the robot, with strange messages popping up one after another.

– LFM raid on the Valley of Procrastination!
– Starting the Chonky Warriurz guild. All dwarf warrs welcome!
– WTS Flag of Libya. PM me.

The robot looked questioningly at the window hanging in the air. MMORPG came to the rescue.

– It's global chat, robot. Better close it.
– All right.
– Oh, by the way, I'm going out for a smoke.

The robot said nothing. While MMORPG was away, a Troll approached the robot and danced the lezginka. A beautiful elf with the username Isabella_69 walked past behind them.

– Oh! Hello, robot! Long time no see, for example!
– Hello… Do we know each other?
– As a matter of fact, don't you recognize me?
– Spider, is that you? What are you doing here?
– Booze can't soothe my sorrow anymore, for example. So I spend my time here.

MMORPG returned.

– I see you're making friends already, robot. So, how do you like it here?
– Sad.
translatorNote: The elf is Sergei 'Spider' Troitsky, using his characteristic verbal tics. The lezginka is a dance from the Caucasus.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Mitzgol
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Mitzgol.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– You just need hypertext FidoNet.
– Hypertext FidoNet? What's that?
– Do you know who Reptilians is?
– What's that got to do with them?
– What do you mean, what's it got to do with them?

Mitzgol looked at the robot in surprise. With a graceful sweep of his gray cloak, the pale overlord departed. Glancing fearfully around, Reptilians appeared from nowhere.

– Hello, robot.
– Do you know where Mitzgol went?
– Probably to get a razor…

Reptilians became sad. Abandoning his pointless attempts to understand what was happening, the robot walked into the sunset.
translatorNote: Mitzgol is a Russian internet persona associated with the proposal for hypertext FidoNet, an older network of bulletin-board systems.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Anime
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Anime. Why are you following me?
– So you won't be sad.
– You aren't helping me get rid of my sadness.
– I help you forget yourself. If you spend more time with me, you'll stop paying attention to your problems.
– But if I forget my sadness, I'll forget myself.

Suddenly a staff flew out of the Void and hit the robot. The robot examined the staff. The character for Tao was carved into it, with a note beside it: 'You've already forgotten yourself.' There were traces of spilled cocoa at one end. The robot turned toward the Living Hedge and said:

– You're right, Taoist-Cocoaist. I must return to the Way.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Visual Novels
text:
The Robot Who Is Sad and Visual Novels

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Visual Novels. Why do I keep coming back to you?
– To find all the endings.
– Is there even one that will stop me being sad?
– Play and find out.

And the robot returned to the world of text, computer graphics and background music. He found himself in a whirlwind of events, feeling the same emotions again and again. When he reached the end, he found himself at the beginning. This continued until every CG was unlocked. Realizing he had witnessed every twist of the plot and could no longer change the characters' fates, the robot sank into That Feel.

– So how are you feeling, robot?
– You already know, Visual Novels.
translatorNote: CGs are the collectible event illustrations in a visual novel.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Music
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Music.
– You look sad, robot.
– You understand me as always, Music.

Heavy sludge riffs fell on the robot from somewhere in the sky, each blow driving sorrow deeper inside. After a little delay, the blurred textures of post-rock joined them. The blue sky spun, dissolving into a whirl of augmented scales.

– Sometimes sadness is all right, robot.

The robot did not answer. He just kept listening.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Hope
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Hope.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Don't worry. Someday it'll pass.
– Why are you so sure, Hope?
– While I'm here, you mustn't give up.

Suddenly Ritochka appeared, cutting through Space, with a sack of sugar over their shoulder. They were drunk and reeked of That Feel the way Camus reeked of Existentialism. Ritochka killed Hope in one stroke. Boarded bus 410. And rode into the sunset. Soon Vikings ran onto the battlefield.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Vikings.
– Who killed Hope, robot? George Martin again?
– It was Ritochka.
– I have more and more competitors!
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Cute Anime Girls
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Cute Anime Girls.
– Have you thought about renaming the community, robot?
– No.
– How about 'The Robot Who Is Sad and Cute Anime Girls'? Authors doesn't seem to be planning to draw anything else.
– Perhaps you're right.

Suddenly a longship sailed across the smooth sea of grass. The Prosecutor of Crimea stepped out.

– None of this nya-meow business!

And tore the mask off Cute Anime Girls. Beneath it was Marketing.

– Oh, I was so close to success!

And giggling foolishly, Marketing ran into the sunset. Left alone with the robot, the Prosecutor of Crimea asked:

– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
translatorNote: The Prosecutor of Crimea refers to Natalia Poklonskaya's 2014 internet popularity and her rejection of the 'nyash-myash' anime-style nickname. Authors remains a singular character, following the Russian canon.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Inconspicuousness
text:
– Hello, robot.

The robot went on his way.

– Hey, robot!

The robot was sad.

– Robot, I'm here!

But the robot remembered the Way and moved steadily toward his goal.

– Why aren't you answering, robot?

The Way is not a trajectory. So the robot could move farther from his destination while drawing closer to the end of the Way.

– Are you kidding me?

Such was the physics of this world. Wherever the robot went, he was always on the Way, and one day he would have to finish it. But the Way was relative. Where one ended, another began.

– ROBOT!

The robot kept walking. Only his Sadness was absolute.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and My Little Pony
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, My Little Pony.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– You need Friendship Magic.
– What's Friendship Magic?
– Follow me. I'll show you.

And the robot went with My Little Pony. Together they drank tea, put on plays and saved the world. But the robot never saw Friendship Magic. Instead, he collected many other questions. Why couldn't he go into the basement that smelled of cupcakes, for instance? Why did My Little Pony keep hiding Rule 34 from the robot? And who was eating all the muffins? When the robot grew tired of this, he decided to leave, and met My Little Pony again.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, My Little Pony.
– Are you leaving already, robot?
– I'd like to, but I don't know how to get out of here.
– The Princess will lower the sun soon.
– I see.

And the robot walked into the sunset.
translatorNote: The basement and muffins refer to My Little Pony fandom stories and memes. Rule 34 is an internet maxim about the existence of adult fan art.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Water
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Water. Where did so much of you come from?
– You know what My Graduation Project is made of, don't you?

The robot knew the answer but said nothing. Space was filling with Water. The Rector hurried into an inflatable boat. The All-Knowing One floated serenely with the help of Onotole's Vest. Soon the robot found himself at Rock Bottom.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Rock Bottom.
– So you've reached me.
– Sad.
translatorNote: In Russian, 'water' also means empty verbiage padding a piece of writing. Onotole's Vest refers to Onotole Wasserman's famous many-pocketed garment.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Chairman of the Globe
text:
– Robot. And work in a ditch. Hello.

A long coat, black with blackness, appeared and humaned itself forward, spitting out the tight puttees of canvas trousers. Smiling absently, it held out a hand shod in a hole-riddled shoe.

– Hello, Chairman of the Globe.
– Will you help me find nails in the dark?
– Should we turn on the light?
– How could I look for nails in the dark then?

The robot found this observation logical and decided to help the poet. The room was tiny and completely empty, and instead of nails they found only sheets covered in scribbles.

– Are these your poems?
– Yes, I write them in the dark when I can't find the nails.
– Is that comfortable?
– No. There's too much furniture here.
– Sad.
translatorNote: Chairman of the Globe was a title used by the Russian Futurist poet Velimir Khlebnikov. The strange wording deliberately echoes experimental poetic language.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and That Guy
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello. Who are you, exactly?
– I'm That Guy!

The robot stared at his companion, trying to remember their face. He felt he had seen this person several times before, but their identity never quite became clear.

– What guy?
– Don't you remember? That Guy! If you need money, I can always lend you some!
– Anything else?
– If you're homesick, I can dress in your mother's clothes.
– That's rather strange.
– If you're sad, I'll always be there!
– As it happens, I'm sad.
– Sorry, but I can't help you.
– Why?
– Because I don't exist.

That Guy evaporated.

– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Gloom
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Gloom.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– That's gloomy.

Space began filling with Gloom. Leaves that the wind had been carrying froze in midair. The falling Ruble's voice grew lower and lower. It became cold. Drops of Gloom formed on surfaces. The motionless figure of Time could be seen against the Living Hedge. The robot felt a gentle nudge in his back. Turning, he saw a staff suspended in the air.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Taoist-Cocoaist.
– You're close to the end now.
– That's sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Professional Humor
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Professional Humor.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– I'll tell you a joke and cheer you up.
– Go ahead.
– Once I ran ldd as root on an unknown executable.
– What's the Point?
– Only a few people understand me.
– Sad.

And as though at the wave of some mysterious hand, Professional Humor found themselves beyond the horizon.
translatorNote: The programmer's joke is that inspecting an untrusted executable with ldd can execute code; doing so as root gives it administrator privileges.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Enthusiasm
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Enthusiasm.
– How did you find me, robot?
– I wasn't looking for you.
– It shows.

For a while the robot and Enthusiasm remained silent. Looking at Enthusiasm more closely, the robot decided to ask a question.

– Why are you naked?
– To be myself, I need nothing but myself. Tell me when you're returning to the Way instead.
– Did Taoist-Cocoaist send you?
– Correct. Did you really think you could find me just like that?
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Simulacrum
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello. I don't know who you are.
– I'm you, robot. Or rather, you're me. Everyone is me.
– Sad.
– I'm a Simulacrum, robot. And you're a Simulacrum. We're all Simulacra.

The robot stared mournfully at the Simulacrum. He began to feel that there were far too many Simulacra around.

– Sadness doesn't exist either, robot. Those who don't exist can't have emotions.

The robot looked around for a bamboo staff, but saw only the Solipsistic Barrel.

– I think I'll go, Simulacrum.
– Just remember that your Way has no meaning.
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and CP
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, CP.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Come with me.
– All right.

The robot spent some Time watching CP, but it could not take away his sadness. Suddenly Roskomnadzor walked past, bubbling loudly with uselessness and stinking of harmfulness.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Roskomnadzor.
– Have you seen CP, robot?
– Yes. Walking around here.
– As long as it isn't circulating on the Internet.

And Roskomnadzor proudly walked into the sunset.
translatorNote: The Russian initials TsP can mean 'central processor' but also have an illicit internet reading; CP recreates that ambiguity in English. Roskomnadzor is Russia's communications and internet regulator.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Paranoia
text:
Paranoia stared wide-eyed at the robot. They were clearly shocked by what they saw.

– Who are you?
– I'm the robot who is sad.
– Why have you come?

The robot looked at Paranoia as though they had lost their mind. He would have liked to know why he had come himself. Paranoia adjusted their very thick glasses and addressed the robot again.

– Did Feminists send you?
– I haven't even spoken to them, Paranoia.
– Why do you give off the same air as Cute Anime Girls, then?

The robot did not answer and walked into the sunset.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Roskomnadzor
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Roskomnadzor.
– I'm blocking you for violating Rule 34, robot.
– Sad.

Roskomnadzor began pounding the air, chopping water and shooting lava. Nothing changed.

– What are you doing, Roskomnadzor?

But Roskomnadzor could no longer hear or see the robot. With a sense of duty fulfilled, they disappeared behind the Living Hedge and lay in wait for a new victim.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Hipster
text:
The robot was quietly shooting at bottles when the Hipster emerged from the sea riding a whale.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Hipster.
– Want me to corner you somewhere dark?
– I think I'll pass.

But the Hipster would not give up and held a photo shoot for the robot. Birds fell to the ground, and for the first time the robot saw Time going backward. The Hipster handed the robot the most successful photograph.

– How do you like it, robot?
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Laziness
text:
– Hello, Laziness.

The robot looked at Laziness and did not know what to do with them. Laziness remained completely indifferent. The robot decided to try talking again.

– Just go.

But Laziness stayed, merely looking silently into the sunset.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Survival
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Survival.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– There's always Hope that you'll stop being sad.
– But Ritochka already killed Hope.

Survival thought for a moment. They did not know how to answer the robot.

– At least you're alive.
– I'm a robot. I'm not alive.
– Then I don't know how to cheer you up.
– Just go.

And Survival walked into a gravitational storm.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Television
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Television.
– Would you like me to tell you something?
– No. I'm sad enough already.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Paper Crane
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Paper Crane.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– If you make a thousand like me, sadness and sorrow will leave you.

Suddenly a flash of Harsh Reality swallowed Space, taking the shape of Lenin. Only a scorched desert remained. The robot turned, but instead of the Paper Crane he saw Decay.

The robot is sad.
The little paper crane turns
To dust in wasteland.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the World
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, World.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– For some reason, I feel like a beginner programmer.
– Many of them come to me first. You could follow the programmer's path too.
– But I can't repair refrigerators and irons.

Somewhere in the Void, a terminal cursor blinked. The robot's hands reached for the keyboard, but a sharp blow from a staff across his fingers knocked away any desire to type even a couple of simple commands.

– Hello, Taoist-Cocoaist.
– You mustn't take another path until you understand this one.
– Sad.
translatorNote: Hello, World is a traditional first program. The refrigerator and iron joke refers to the expectation that programmers can fix any electrical appliance.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the PR Manager
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, PR Manager.
– You didn't ask, of course, but I'm getting closer to arranging a meeting for you with Popularity.
– Are you a friend of Marketing's?
– We studied together. But while Marketing thinks words alone can achieve anything, I do actual work.
– Why?
– So you'll have more Readers.
– But I don't need that.
– Neither Authors nor I planned to ask you.
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and CAPTCHA
text:
– Hello, CAPTCHA.
– Prove that you are not a robot.
– I'm sad.
– Enter the text you see in the image.

The robot looked at the image, but saw only an unrecognizable mess. It reminded him of ancient runes, so he decided to ask Vikings for help. The moment the robot thought of this, a lively longship appeared on the horizon. Soon it was beside him.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Vikings.
– Is something wrong, robot? I suddenly felt you needed help.
– Yes. Can you solve CAPTCHA?

Vikings began examining the image closely. Suddenly they took out an axe and killed CAPTCHA without the slightest hesitation.

– Why did you kill CAPTCHA, Vikings?
– I couldn't read it. If I don't understand something, it's easier to destroy it.
– Sad.
